name: Everolimus (GI/pancreatic NET)
histology: well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (low or intermediate grade)

biomarkers.note: Everolimus (mTOR inhibitor) is a category 1 option for progressive well-differentiated advanced NET (gastrointestinal, pancreatic, and lung primaries in the RADIANT program). Unlike somatostatin analogues and PRRT, everolimus activity is not SSTR-dependent. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors, and DeVita 12th ed.

lineOfTherapy: option for progressive well-differentiated advanced NET (category 1 for progressive disease); not strictly line-scoped

eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v1.2026, neuroendocrine line 4962 (Everolimus, category 1 for progressive disease, 10 mg by mouth daily)

drugs.name: Everolimus

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors
provenance.locator: neuroendocrine line 4962 (Everolimus, category 1 for progressive disease, 10 mg by mouth, daily); line 7992 (everolimus administered orally at a dose of 10 mg once daily)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) NET v1.2026 (neuroendocrine lines 4962, 7992). Everolimus 10 mg PO once daily, given continuously (days 1 to 28 of a 28-day cycle). No ISMP tall-man form. Everolimus-specific monitoring: stomatitis/oral ulcers, non-infectious pneumonitis, hyperglycemia and hyperlipidemia, infections, and myelosuppression.

supportiveCare: Continuous daily oral dosing; continue until progression or intolerance.
Prophylactic/therapeutic management of stomatitis (e.g., corticosteroid mouthwash) reduces everolimus-associated oral ulceration.
Monitor fasting glucose and lipids; screen for and manage non-infectious pneumonitis.

monitoring: pulmonary symptoms / non-infectious pneumonitis (imaging if symptomatic)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2-3 stomatitis, non-infectious pneumonitis, or metabolic toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Hold and resume at a reduced dose (e.g., 5 mg daily) per labeling; for grade 3-4 pneumonitis discontinue and obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: everolimus established as an mTOR inhibitor with activity in progressive well-differentiated NET (RADIANT program); per-cycle dose carried from the guideline layer

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors
guideline.locator: neuroendocrine lines 4962 (Everolimus category 1 for progressive disease, 10 mg by mouth daily), 7992 (10 mg once daily)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for everolimus in well-differentiated GI/pancreatic NET (disease #30). Everolimus 10 mg PO once daily continuously is dose-grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) NET v1.2026 (neuroendocrine lines 4962 and 7992; category 1 for progressive disease). Biomarker gate: well-differentiated NET with progression (everolimus is not SSTR-dependent, unlike SSA and PRRT). No dose was invented or inferred and no field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
